Slopes of a Covariate by Group

Source: R/pm_slopes.R
pm_slopes.Rd

The slope (rate of change) of the fitted response in a numeric covariate within each level of a model term, with standard errors, degrees of freedom, confidence limits and tests, and pairwise comparisons of the slopes, as emmeans::emtrends() and SAS ESTIMATE statements on slope terms.

Usage

pm_slopes(model, covariate, modelterm, at = NULL, level = 0.05, adj = "none",
          df_method = c("auto", "Kenward-Roger", "Satterthwaite", "containment", "between-within", "KR-SAS"),
          vcov_adjust = TRUE,
          weights = c("equal", "proportional", "outer", "cells", "flat"), vcov = NULL)

Arguments

model

A fitted model, as for predictmeans.

covariate

Name (in "quotes") of the numeric covariate.

modelterm

Name (in "quotes") of the factor term whose levels get a slope each, e.g. "Variety".

at

The value of the covariate where the slopes are taken (matters only when the covariate enters the model non-linearly); the default is its mean.

level

Significance level for the confidence limits, the default is 0.05.

adj

Adjustment of the p-values of the pairwise comparisons of slopes, as in predictmeans.

df_method, vcov_adjust, weights, vcov

As in predictmeans.

Value

A list of two data frames:

slopes

one row per level of modelterm: the factor columns, slope, std.error, df, conf.low, conf.high, statistic (t) and p.value (of slope = 0).

pairs

one row per pair of levels: level1, level2, estimate (slope of level1 minus slope of level2), std.error, df, statistic, p.value and p.adj.

Details

The slopes are on the scale of the linear predictor. They come from the reference grid of Kmatrix: the change in the K matrix between at - h and at + h, divided by 2h with h = 0.0001 times the standard deviation of the covariate. This is exact when the covariate enters the model linearly (also through interactions) and a central difference for poly(), splines and smooths, whose slope depends on at. Standard errors and degrees of freedom follow predictmeans: for lmer models fitted by REML Kenward-Roger (with the adjusted covariance when vcov_adjust = TRUE), for lme the smallest nlme df of the terms with the covariate, otherwise the residual df.

Author

Dongwen Luo, Siva Ganesh and John Koolaard

Examples

  library(predictmeans)
  Oats <- as.data.frame(nlme::Oats)
  fm <- lmer(yield ~ nitro*Variety + (1|Block/Variety), data = Oats)
  pm_slopes(fm, "nitro", "Variety")
#> Slopes of ‘nitro’ at 0.3 
#> 
#>      Variety slope std.error df conf.low conf.high statistic   p.value
#>  Golden Rain 75.33     11.86 51    51.53     99.14     6.353 5.726e-08
#>   Marvellous 64.58     11.86 51    40.78     88.39     5.446 1.490e-06
#>      Victory 81.08     11.86 51    57.28    104.89     6.838 9.828e-09
#> 
#> Pairwise differences of slopes (p.adj: none)
#> 
#>       level1     level2 estimate std.error df statistic p.value  p.adj
#>  Golden Rain Marvellous    10.75     16.77 51    0.6410  0.5244 0.5244
#>  Golden Rain    Victory    -5.75     16.77 51   -0.3429  0.7331 0.7331
#>   Marvellous    Victory   -16.50     16.77 51   -0.9839  0.3298 0.3298
